shots.caption: MK classes and luminosity classes at equal distance; colour = blackbody chromaticity of Teff; radius compressed as R^0.35
Resolved G2 V photosphere: limb darkening u≈0.6, illustrative granulation
Red supergiant: cool (≈3500 K class-typical), strongly limb-darkened, few giant convection cells (illustrative)
Io shadow transit, 2026-11-10 01:20 UTC — positions from the shared Kepler engine; penumbra from the Sun's true angular size; Jupiter map: Solar System Scope (CC BY 4.0)
Galilean moons at their computed positions for the same instant (true sizes and distances, 1 unit = 1000 km)
True relative sizes (JPL mean radii); USGS/NASA mosaics (Moon: Solar System Scope CC BY 4.0); Lommel–Seeliger regolith; Titan = haze model, no surface map
The Moon: maria and highlands from the albedo map; regolith photometry (Lommel–Seeliger) gives the flat-looking disk and sharp terminator
Europa: Galileo/Voyager mosaic (USGS) — lineae and chaos terrain
Titan: forward-scattering orange photochemical haze (single-scattering model, illustrative coefficients) hides the surface
Earth: Rayleigh+Mie single scattering (blue limb, reddened terminator), night lights only on the dark side; maps: Solar System Scope (CC BY 4.0)
Atmospheric limb at the terminator
Schwarzschild ray tracing: shadow, photon ring and the lensed far side of the disk arching over and under the hole; approaching side brighter and bluer (Doppler beaming)
Same model at 50° inclination
EDUCATIONAL: relativistic jets as a Doppler-boosted emission cone (not a jet-physics model)
Volumetric H II region (ILLUSTRATIVE density field): Hα 656 nm red, [O III] 501 nm teal near the hottest stars, dust lanes in extinction, cavity carved around the cluster
Inside the volume: parallax and depth between dust columns that point toward the ionising stars
Grand-design spiral (Sb-like, illustrative parameters): exponential disk, log-spiral arms (pitch 14°), Hernquist bulge, blue arms / yellow bulge, Hα knots, dust on the inner arm edges
Barred spiral (SBb-like): arms start at the bar ends
Elliptical E3: Hernquist (de Vaucouleurs-like) profile, smooth old red population, no dust lanes
Irregular (Magellanic-type): clumpy star formation, no global symmetry
Dwarf spheroidal: diffuse Plummer sphere, low surface brightness
Interacting pair from a restricted three-body simulation (Toomre & Toomre 1972): tidal tails and bridge form from gravity alone
Lighthouse model: neutron star, inclined magnetic dipole (field lines r = L sin²θ), beams along the magnetic axis — EDUCATIONAL depiction; rotation slowed ×300 (Crab P ≈ 33.7 ms)
Same pulsar at the rotation phase where a beam sweeps across the observer: the pulse
Phobos: triaxial shape from the catalogue (Thomas et al., scaled to the JPL mean radius); craters and grooves PROCEDURAL (not mapped); albedo ≈ 0.07
Generic S-type-like asteroid: irregular procedural shape, crater size distribution N(>D) ∝ D⁻²
Comet at 1 AU: curved dust tail (grains under gravity reduced by radiation pressure, 1−β) and straight blue ion tail (solar wind) — both simulated; nucleus enlarged for visibility
Dark bilobed nucleus (albedo ≈ 0.04, illustrative shape) inside its coma
